headline: ECB's Lagarde warns AI debt concentration could spill into euro area markets
body: ECB President Christine Lagarde told the European Parliament's economic affairs committee on September 28 that global equity valuations are concentrated in a small number of AI-related firms rapidly increasing their debt funding, and a sharp reassessment of their prospects could trigger market corrections that spill over to euro area investors. She said euro area firms will devote around 10% of total investment to AI this year, with AI-related borrowing already a quarter of firms' credit growth.
note: A quarter of credit growth to firms tied to one asset class is a concentration number worth sitting with. Emerging-market supervisors far from Frankfurt should note that a reassessment of AI valuations in the US or Europe would not stay contained there.

evidence.text: Firms are set to devote around 10% of total investment to AI in 2026, and AI-related borrowing already accounts for roughly a quarter of credit growth to firms.

Global equity valuations are concentrated in a relatively small number of AI-related firms, which are also rapidly increasing their debt funding. A sharp reassessment of AI companies’ prospects and the sustainability of their debt could trigger market corrections and spill over to euro area investors and the wider economy.

Europe should strengthen underdeveloped critical parts of the AI value chain. Building European capacity will also ensure that we can rely on European tech for sensitive activities – in line with the aim of the Technological Sovereignty Package.
